territorial_scope.description: Applies to cyberviolence acts carried out within the PRC and reaches overseas organisations and individuals whose acts target the PRC.

evidence.quote: 境外的组织、个人针对中华人民共和国境内实施的网络暴力活动，依照本法有关规定处理和追究责任。

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Draft PRC anti-cyberviolence law, released for public comment on 29 July 2026. Defines cyberviolence; imposes detection, removal, real-name and complaint duties on online service providers; restricts AI-enabled cyberviolence; sets government coordination, court injunctions and penalties. Effective date blank in draft.
summary.long: Draft Anti-Cyberviolence Law (60 articles, seven chapters) published by the Cyberspace Administration of China for public comment on 29 July 2026, with comments due 28 August 2026. It defines cyberviolence as concentrated or continuous online infringement of reputation, honour, privacy, portrait rights or personal information (Art. 2), and applies to such acts within China and to overseas actors targeting China (Art. 3). Chapter 2 imposes duties on online service providers: internal management systems, real-name verification for information-posting and instant-messaging services (Art. 12), AI-assisted and human monitoring, a bar on algorithmic recommendation of risk content, risk labels, self-protection settings, takedown and account restrictions, rumour refutation, and complaint and appeal channels. Large platforms must run rapid-response mechanisms, annual risk assessments and publish annual reports (Art. 21). Chapter 3 assigns coordination to national and local cyberspace authorities alongside public security and other departments. Prohibited conduct includes AI-enabled cyberviolence (Art. 31) and aiding it (Art. 32). Courts may issue personality-right injunctions (Art. 37), public security may issue warning letters to offenders (Art. 40), and prosecutors may bring public-interest suits (Art. 43). Penalties include warnings, fines, business suspension and joint civil liability (Arts. 47-54). The effective date (Art. 60) is left blank.

relations.note: Art. 57 assigns civil liability for damage caused by organising, inciting or aiding online violence 'according to' the Civil Code and other laws; the draft does not set out the civil liability rules itself.

notes: Consultation draft (征求意见稿) of 60 articles in seven chapters, published by CAC on 2026-07-29 with comments due 2026-08-28; the document is the CAC notice page including the draft text and an explanatory note. Art. 60 (effective date) is left blank ('自 年 月 日起施行'). Penalty articles 47 to 49 cite specific articles of this draft; Arts. 50 and 55 defer to other laws and regulations without naming them. The explanatory note cites the NPC Standing Committee 2026 legislative work plan as the drafting basis; that plan is not a legal basis in the bill text and is not coded as a relation. Entities are public bodies only; network service providers are the main addressees but are a class, not named firms.

evidence.quote: 应当创新宣传方式

obligations.summary: Network service providers shall establish and improve anti-cyberviolence systems covering registration, account management, personal information, review, monitoring, handling and complaints; publish management rules and platform pacts; and sign service agreements with users.

evidence.quote: 应当建立健全网络暴力监测识别机制

evidence.quote: 不得利用算法推荐等技术推送相关信息

obligations.conditional_on: where a cyberviolence risk is found

evidence.quote: 对异常账号进行真实身份信息动态核验

obligations.summary: Providers shall report to the relevant authorities when browsing, search, comment or report volumes on related content grow significantly.
obligations.conditional_on: where browsing, search, comment or report volumes related to content grow significantly

evidence.quote: 还应当及时向有关部门报告

evidence.quote: 按照国家有关规定落实人工智能生成合成内容标识等制度

obligations.summary: Providers shall establish anti-cyberviolence protection functions and options, such as blocking strangers or specific users and prohibiting reposting or commenting on one's posts.

evidence.quote: 建立健全网络暴力防护功能，提供便利用户设置屏蔽陌生用户或者特定用户

obligations.summary: Providers shall give protection guidance and rescue services to users facing risk; live-streaming, audio-video and social network providers shall serve minors through a minors mode and offer guardians risk alerts and usage information.
obligations.conditional_on: where cyberviolence risk may harm minors, elderly or disabled users, or cause personal or property damage

evidence.quote: 应当为用户提供网络暴力防护指导和保护救助服务

obligations.summary: Providers shall report such risks to CAC and public security authorities and report leads on cyberviolence crimes to public security.
obligations.conditional_on: where cyberviolence risk may harm users or cause serious consequences

evidence.quote: 并向网信、公安等有关部门报告

obligations.summary: Providers shall refine classification and identification rules for cyberviolence information for their services, following the national classification standard.

evidence.quote: 细化所提供服务相关网络暴力信息分类和识别规则

evidence.quote: 应当依法及时采取必要的措施制止网络暴力活动

obligations.summary: Providers shall establish a rumour-refutation mechanism and take refutation measures against false or misleading cyberviolence information.

evidence.quote: 应当建立健全辟谣机制

evidence.quote: 应当建立健全用户账号分类分级管理制度

evidence.quote: 应当建立健全网络暴力快速响应机制

obligations.conditional_on: platform with a huge number of users or significant influence on users

enforcement.authority: 网信、电信、公安部门和其他有关主管部门 (cyberspace, telecom, public security and other competent departments)
enforcement.triggered_by: Network service providers violating Art. 11 or Art. 36
enforcement.max_penalty_text: 处五万元以上五十万元以下罚款 (fine of 50,000 to 500,000 yuan, where the provider refuses to correct or the case is serious); earlier steps: warning, correction order, confiscation of illegal gains

enforcement.penalty_formula: Order to correct, warning or criticism by notice, fine of 50,000 to 500,000 yuan may be added; if refusal or serious case, fine of 500,000 to 2,000,000 yuan; if particularly serious impact or consequences, fine of 2,000,000 to 10,000,000 yuan; may also be ordered to suspend business, suspend for rectification, close the website or app, or revoke licences; directly responsible persons fined 50,000 to 200,000 yuan (50,000 to 200,000 yuan in the refusal tier; 50,000 to 200,000 yuan for directly responsible persons)

evidence.quote: 造成特别严重影响、特别严重后果的，由有关主管部门处二百万元以上一千万元以下罚款

enforcement.cure_period: Order to correct within a time limit (length not stated)

evidence.quote: 依照有关法律、行政法规的规定处罚

enforcement.penalty_formula: Warning, order to correct within a time limit, clearing of subscribed accounts, restriction of functions, suspension or restriction of profit-making rights, suspension of services, closure of account or ban on re-registration; fine of 100,000 to 500,000 yuan may be added
enforcement.cure_period: Order to correct within a time limit (length not stated)

evidence.quote: 可以并处十万元以上五十万元以下罚款

enforcement.penalty_formula: Order to correct; if refusal or serious case, disciplinary sanctions on directly responsible supervisory personnel and other directly responsible persons (no amount stated)
enforcement.cure_period: Order to correct (time limit not stated)

evidence.quote: 拒不改正或者情节严重的，对直接负责的主管人员和其他直接责任人员依法给予处分

evidence.quote: 应当予以批评教育、劝诫制止

enforcement.triggered_by: Network service providers who knew or should have known of network violence by a user, did not take necessary measures in time, or helped others carry it out

enforcement.penalty_formula: Joint and several civil liability with the network user

evidence.quote: 依法与该网络用户承担连带责任

enforcement.penalty_reference: Civil Code of the PRC (cited by name)

evidence.quote: 网络暴力侵害自然人人身权益造成严重精神损害的，被侵权人有权请求精神损害赔偿

thresholds.note: The draft contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Scope and tiers are set by qualitative terms (用户数量巨大或者对用户具有显著影响, 较大影响力, 严重情节, 特别严重). The fine amounts in Arts. 47-51 are enforcement, not thresholds. The age and disability categories (未成年人, 残疾人, 老年人) carry no numeric limit.
